title: IRGNN: A Graph-based Framework Integrating Numerical Solution and Point Cloud for Static IR Drop Prediction
problem: IR drop analysis in on-chip power grids is computationally expensive; traditional numerical methods are accurate but slow, while CNN-based ML methods lose fine-grained topology and PG structure information.
method: IRGNN combines numerical solver (AMG-PCG) to generate rough solutions as ground truth with graph-based learning: treats PG nodes as point clouds, extracts features via graph transformer and novel Neighbor Distance Attention (NDA) layer for distance-aware aggregation, capturing both local and global PG topology.

title: X-SAT: An Efficient Circuit-Based SAT Solver
problem: Verifying equivalence of arithmetic circuits requires efficient SAT solving, but existing SAT solvers optimized for CNF struggle with circuit-specific structure and the high variable/clause counts in complex arithmetic circuits.
method: X-SAT integrates Conflict-Driven Clause Learning (CDCL) with structural elimination techniques that reduce variables and clauses while preserving circuit topology. It enhances branching heuristics specifically for arithmetic circuit structure to guide search more efficiently.

title: Helix: Serving Large Language Models over Heterogeneous GPUs and Network via Max-Flow
problem: Serving LLMs across heterogeneous GPU clusters (differing GPU types, memory capacities, and interconnect speeds) is inefficient because existing systems cannot jointly optimize model placement and request scheduling to account for both GPU and network heterogeneity simultaneously.
method: Helix models the LLM inference computation over a heterogeneous cluster as a max-flow problem on a directed, weighted graph where nodes represent GPU instances and edge capacities encode both GPU compute throughput and network bandwidth. A Mixed Integer Linear Programming (MILP) solver operates on this graph to jointly discover optimized model placement (which layers/shards go where) and request scheduling (how tokens are routed through the cluster), treating the two tasks as a unified optimization rather than solving them independently.

title: LLMs Meet Post-Silicon Test Engineering: A New Era (Invited)
problem: Post-silicon test engineering requires domain-specific expertise; AI automation of test tasks is limited by lack of domain grounding.
method: Two-stage LLM-based AI agent framework for post-silicon test engineering: (1) reasoning stage interprets user queries using LLM capabilities, (2) grounding stage executes tasks by integrating LLM outputs with existing test infrastructure. Case study: Intelligent Engineering Assistant (IEA) demonstrates autonomous task execution within established test framework.

title: When Mitigations Backfire: Timing Channel Attacks and Defense for PRAC-Based RowHammer Mitigations
problem: The JEDEC DDR5 Per Row Activation Counting (PRAC) mechanism and its Alert Back-Off (ABO) protocol and Refresh Management (RFM) commands introduce observable timing differences that create a new timing side-channel, allowing attackers to monitor memory access latencies and infer sensitive information such as cryptographic keys.
method: The paper first presents PRACLeak, a timing channel attack that exploits latency variations induced by ABO protocol and RFM commands to extract secret keys from vulnerable AES implementations by monitoring memory access timing. To counter this, the authors propose Timing-Safe PRAC (TPRAC), which replaces activity-triggered RFM commands with Timing-Based RFMs issued periodically and independently of memory activity, eliminating the observable correlation between memory access patterns and mitigation timing. TPRAC requires only a single-entry in-DRAM mitigation queue per bank and is designed to be compatible with existing DRAM standards.

title: MiniWear: Minimizing Flash Wear via Hybrid Persistent Cache for Extended EF-SMR Lifetime
problem: EF-SMR (Embedded-Flash SMR) systems combine NAND flash and Shingled Magnetic Recording disks to balance cost/performance, but flash endurance faces critical degradation due to high traffic-to-capacity ratios causing excessive wear.
method: MiniWear introduces a hybrid persistent cache (PC) composed of Flash-PC and SMR-PC tiers with fine-grained scheduling strategies. At hardware level, the PC is organized as dual tiers; at software level, customized scheduling manages PC resources efficiently. Proactive balancing strategy addresses resource idleness to maximize wear distribution across storage layers.

title: 5.1 A GaN SLCG-Doherty-Continuum Power Amplifier Achieving >38% 6dB Back-Off Efficiency Over 1.35 to 7.6GHz
problem: Wireless systems with hundreds of MHz bandwidth and complex modulations (high PAPR) require power amplifiers with large RF bandwidth, high back-off efficiency, good linearity, and compact size; gallium nitride (GaN) technology offers high power density but efficiency degrades significantly at back-off.
method: The GaN power amplifier implements a series-load conducting Gallium Nitride (SLCG) combined with Doherty-Continuum architecture to achieve high efficiency across wide frequencies (1.35-7.6GHz) and power back-off conditions.

title: DuoQ: A DSP Utilization-aware and Outlier-free Quantization for FPGA-based LLMs Acceleration
problem: Quantization for FPGA-based LLM acceleration faces challenges from quantization outliers affecting accuracy. Existing methods use expensive channel-wise or token-wise isolation and encoding for outlier handling.
method: DuoQ introduces learnable equivalent transformations and low-semantic token awareness eliminating outliers while enabling per-tensor 4-bit quantization. Algorithm-hardware co-design includes DSP-aware processing element (PE) unit and encoder, plus post-processing units for nonlinear functions and dynamic token awareness.

title: Late Breaking Results: Versatile 4:1 Multiplexer Using 1T1R RRAM Crossbar for High Speed In-Memory Computing
problem: In-memory computing with RRAM crossbars requires efficient logic operations, but existing 4:1 multiplexer designs require 10 steps, limiting the speed of computations performed directly in memory.
method: The paper proposes a NAND-based 4:1 multiplexer design in a 1T1R RRAM crossbar that completes execution in 3 steps instead of 10. The approach extends to full adders, full subtractors, and 1-bit comparators, reducing clock cycles by 75% compared to state-of-the-art designs. Although memristor count increases, the computational delay reduction makes this promising for in-memory computing.

title: PatternPaint: Practical Layout Pattern Generation Using Diffusion-Based Inpainting
problem: VLSI layout pattern generation requires large, design-rule-compliant training datasets; new technology nodes lack such data, making existing training-based methods impractical.
method: PatternPaint uses diffusion-based inpainting with few-shot fine-tuning on pretrained image models; template-based denoising simplifies generation into inpainting tasks. Fine-tuning requires only 20 design-rule-compliant samples.

title: 3.1 A 121.3dB-DR, 115dB-PSNR, Digital-Input Capacitive-Feedback Class-D Audio Amplifier with Double-Sided Voltage-Boosting (DSVB) Modulation
problem: Class-D audio amplifiers are limited in output power by battery voltage; prior approaches achieve boost via 2-stage DC-DC conversion (inefficient, ~80%) or single-stage buck-boost (limited dynamic range), struggling to combine high dynamic range (>120dB) with high efficiency and small form-factor.
method: Double-sided voltage-boosting (DSVB) modulation integrating capacitive-feedback chopper-amplifier with single-inductor buck-boost power stage, achieving high dynamic range (121.3dB DR) with 87% efficiency and only one off-chip inductor via single-stage power delivery.

title: BlockPIM: Optimizing Memory Management for PIM-enabled Long-Context LLM Inference
problem: PIM architectures alleviate memory bandwidth bottlenecks in LLM decode phase but fragmented data layout limits end-to-end acceleration, especially for long-context sequences where memory utilization remains suboptimal.
method: Proposes cross-channel block memory layout strategy maximizing utilization and eliminating context length constraints; introduces cross-channel attention computation compatible with current PIM architecture to support distributed operations.

title: A Novel Image-Graph Heterogeneous Fusion Framework for Static IR Drop Prediction
problem: IR drop analysis is critical for IC reliability but computationally challenging at ultra-deep-submicron scales. Current CNN-based approaches neglect power delivery network (PDN) global spatial features and cell-instance topological information.
method: Image-Graph Heterogeneous Fusion (IGHF) framework combining CNN and GNN branches. CNN branch (Power ScaleFusion UNet) uses Long-range Local-detail Encoder (LLE) and Hierarchical Adjacent Compensation Group (HACG) for multi-scale spatial power feature extraction and adaptive fusion. GNN branch uses Cell Voltage Aware (CVA) module to aggregate PDN topological features from heterogeneous neighbors. Transfer learning enables few-shot adaptation to real circuits.

title: DAWN: Accelerating Point Cloud Object Detection via Object-Aware Partitioning and 3D Similarity-Based Filtering
problem: Point cloud object detection for autonomous driving and robotics faces high computational cost due to complex point processing on large per-frame point sets.
method: DAWN identifies frame-to-frame similarities and filters redundant points through object-aware partitioning based on previous detection results. Axis-sorted point selection refines partitioning for non-uniform point distributions. Efficient 3D similarity algorithm performs point filtering. Flexible latency-accuracy tradeoffs via configurable filtering ratios.

title: MMDFL: Multi-Model-based Decentralized Federated Learning for Resource-Constrained AIoT Systems
problem: Decentralized federated learning on resource-constrained AIoT devices faces challenges from limited computing/bandwidth, non-IID data, and expensive all-neighbor aggregation.
method: MMDFL uses multiple traveler models performing local training across devices, with adaptive device selection based on data heterogeneity and resource availability. Knowledge aggregation is decoupled from full neighborhood dependencies.

title: Enterprise Class Modular Cache Hierarchy
problem: Enterprise mission-critical workloads demand cache hierarchies that deliver consistent low-latency performance at sustained processor utilization above 90% across diverse and highly virtualized workloads, while remaining extensible across processor generations and new technology insertions.
method: The IBM Telum and Telum II processors introduce a modular, horizontally federated cache hierarchy in which last-level cache slices are distributed across chiplets and interconnected through high-bandwidth on-chip links. An adaptive horizontal cache persistence algorithm dynamically adjusts which cache levels retain hot data across different access patterns and workload phases. The paper details how fetch events flow through this hierarchy and how cache size changes affect system-level performance, culminating in the Telum II design that simultaneously supports traditional enterprise workloads and generative AI inference.
